legalName: Motion to Vacate a Void Drug Possession Conviction and Refund Paid Legal Financial Obligations, State v. Blake
publicName: Vacate a Washington drug possession conviction that is void, and get your money back
mechanism: Blake relief rests on the conviction being unconstitutionally void rather than on any waiting period or clean record. It covers convictions based on RCW 69.50.4013 or RCW 69.50.4014, their predecessor statutes, similar local ordinances, and certain inchoate offences, which the Blake order forms state are unconstitutionally void and must be vacated, with legal financial obligations and accrued interest paid pursuant to those convictions refunded. The relief available is vacation, refund of paid legal financial obligations, waiver of unpaid balances, and full or partial case vacatur, in superior, district and municipal courts alike. The refund is the part participants most often do not know about. Blake is not the same as the RCW 9.96.060(6) treatment route: Blake is about a void conviction and the treatment route is about treatment or programme participation, and the same person may qualify for both, so both questions are asked.
exclusions: Convictions not based on RCW 69.50.4013, RCW 69.50.4014, their predecessors, a similar local ordinance, or a covered inchoate offence.
Convictions for offences other than simple possession, including possession with intent to deliver and delivery.
Any expectation that the refund is automatic; it is claimed.

waitingPeriods.duration: None. Eligibility turns on the void conviction category, not on any elapsed period.

venue: The sentencing court, which may be superior, district or municipal. The Blake form set includes separate superior court and courts-of-limited-jurisdiction instruments, including partial vacate orders.

destination.detail: File the Blake motion and the matching order in the court that entered the conviction. Where the case included other charges, a partial vacate order is used. The refund of paid legal financial obligations and accrued interest is claimed with the motion.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Washington State Patrol criminal history record. The $11 WATCH name and date-of-birth check online gives conviction information immediately and is enough to start routing. The non-conviction record is a different and slower product: it needs a fingerprint card plus $12, or an in-person record review at no fee with fingerprints and limited inspection time. Read the WSP fee table live rather than relying on a stored figure.

Check your answer to "What were you convicted of, and which exact RCW or municipal ordinance was it under?" against Washington State Patrol criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Court docket from the sentencing court. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for the docket. It supplies the cause number, the exact RCW, the offence class, the sentencing date and the supervision and release dates. Every Washington waiting period runs from one of those dates and none of them is reliably on the $11 WATCH check.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the district, municipal or superior court that sentenced the participant

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "What is the sentencing date, the date you were released from any confinement, and the date any supervision or probation ended?" against Court docket from the sentencing court, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Payment history for the case. Ask the clerk, or the collections agency the court used, for a full payment history on the cause number. The refund is of what you actually paid plus accrued interest, so the payment history is what the claim is built on.

generationRequirements.question: What is your full legal name, and any other name the case was filed under?
What is your date of birth?
What were you convicted of, and which exact RCW or municipal ordinance was it under?
Which court sentenced you — district, municipal or superior — and in which county or city?
What is the sentencing date, the date you were released from any confinement, and the date any supervision or probation ended?
Do you have any charge pending anywhere — Washington, another state, federal court or tribal court?
Have you been convicted of any new crime since, in this state, another state, or federal or tribal court?
Was the conviction for simple drug possession, and under which statute or local ordinance?
Were there other charges in the same case that are not drug possession?
Did you pay any fines, fees, costs or restitution on this case, and roughly how much?
Is any balance still owed on this case?
Separately from Blake: have you completed a substance use disorder programme, or been assessed by a recovery navigator, arrest and jail alternative, or LEAD programme?

selfHelpBoundaries: Any pending charge in Washington, another state, federal court, or tribal court.
Any domestic violence element, charged or findable from the court file.
Any protection, no-contact, antiharassment or civil restraining order currently in effect, or violated in the last five years.
Any DUI, physical control, or alcohol or drug related driving offence, including a reduced charge.
Any firearm, deadly weapon or sexual motivation enhancement.
Any question about offence class or the exact RCW.
Any participant whose real goal is firearm rights restoration, which is a separate proceeding under RCW 9.41.041.
The conviction may not be simple possession, since possession with intent and delivery are outside Blake.
The case included other charges and it is unclear whether a full or partial vacatur is right.
The participant is chasing a refund from a court that has already refunded it, or through a collections agency that disputes the payment history.
packetInstructions: The refund side is the part participants most often do not know about.
Vacation does not make the court record private, or remove the case from court indexes and public court websites. Never call Washington vacation expungement.
Vacation does not restore firearm rights, which run through RCW 9.41.041.

Vacated convictions still count for recidivist charging. RCW 9.96.060(8)(c) provides that a conviction vacated on or after 2019-07-28 qualifies as a prior conviction for the purpose of charging a present recidivist offense committed on or after that date.
Local county superior court rules may require additional documents. Every packet carries a local-check instruction rather than assuming the pattern form set is complete.
participantQuestions: Interaction with WA-VAC-04: the same person may qualify for both. Blake is about a void conviction; RCW 9.96.060(6) is about treatment or program participation. Ask both questions.
